options.D: They must volunteer for the study

explanation: Spot on. To be a 'case', the person must actually meet the medical criteria for the specific condition we are investigating.

question: An adolescent daughter tells the nurse she is exhausted from missing school to look after her sick mother. What should the nurse recognize?

options.A: The family is experiencing role strain and needs additional support
options.B: The teenager is simply misbehaving and needs stricter discipline
options.C: The mother's illness has cured itself through natural rest
options.D: Normal adolescent development includes full-time caregiving

explanation: When children take on heavy caregiving roles, it signals that the family system is strained and requires outside intervention. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h4)

question: What type of computer is the bedside tablet you use for clinical charting?

options.A: Mainframe
options.B: Microcomputer
options.C: Supercomputer
options.D: Analog processor

explanation: Tablets, laptops, and desktop PCs are all types of microcomputers (or personal computers) built for everyday tasks.

question: In nursing management, what do we mean by conflict "antecedents"?

options.A: The official disciplinary policies used after a fight occurs
options.B: The underlying conditions that create fertile ground for disputes
options.C: The emotional reactions patients have to hospital staff
options.D: The legal documents signed when a nurse is hired

explanation: Think of antecedents as the early sparks or background conditions that set the stage for a disagreement to happen later. Spotting them early helps you keep the ward peaceful!

question: Why is it best to use both quantitative and qualitative methods during your community assessment?

options.A: It is required by law to spend extra ministry funding
options.B: It prevents nurses from having to speak to villagers directly
options.C: It combines measurable statistics with deep human context
options.D: It ensures that no written reports need to be created

explanation: Numbers give you the stats (how many people are sick), but talking to people gives you the story (why they are sick and what stops them from getting help). You need both!

question: What is the main goal of a two-way referral system in mental health care?

options.A: To permanently transfer all chronic clients to tertiary psychiatric hospitals
options.B: To reduce the total number of medications prescribed at primary clinics
options.C: To ensure smooth movement of clients and feedback between different levels of care
options.D: To allow primary nurses to independently diagnose complex psychiatric disorders

explanation: Think of a two-way referral as a team effort between clinics and big hospitals. It keeps communication flowing both ways so no patient is left stranded in the system!

question: Why do we call bones a living organ system instead of just dry structures?

options.A: It changes its shape solely due to external pressure from tight clothing
options.B: It is made entirely of soft muscle tissue that continuously moves on its own
options.C: It contains active cells, blood vessels, and nerves that respond to the body's needs
options.D: It grows larger only by absorbing water from the surrounding skin tissues

explanation: You got this! Bones aren't just dead sticks; they are packed with blood and nerves so they can repair themselves and react to stress.

question: Using the ROME mnemonic (Respiratory Opposite, Metabolic Equal), how do pH and bicarbonate ($HCO_3^-$) move in a metabolic imbalance?

options.A: They move in opposite directions
options.B: They move in the same direction
options.C: They cancel each other out instantly
options.D: They remain completely unchanged

explanation: ROME helps us remember: in metabolic issues, the pH and bicarbonate are Equal (they move in the same direction—both go up or both go down). You've got this!

question: A nursing mother says she cannot afford expensive baby formula or imported supplements. As a nurse, what is your best response?

options.A: Explain that homemade food has no nutritional value for babies
options.B: Show her how to enrich local family staples with mashed beans and green leaves
options.C: Advise her to wait until the child is five years old to eat solid food
options.D: Tell her to stop breastfeeding immediately and buy cow milk instead

explanation: Wonderful nursing care! Always encourage affordable, locally available foods that families can easily prepare and sustain.

question: What is the primary role of the nurse regarding drug hazards?

options.A: Serving as the final safety barrier before administration
options.B: Manufacturing safer pharmaceutical compounds for hospital use
options.C: Determining the exact chemical composition of all prescribed drugs
options.D: Prescribing alternative medications to avoid dangerous side effects

explanation: Nurses check medications right before giving them to catch errors made earlier in the process. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h1)

question: How full can a sharps box get before you must close and replace it?

options.A: One-quarter full
options.B: Completely packed to the top rim
options.C: Whenever it starts smelling bad
options.D: Three-quarters full

explanation: Safety first! Always seal and replace sharps containers when they are three-quarters full so needles don't poke out and accidentally injure someone.

question: Why is the evaluation phase considered important for future public health work?

options.A: It provides lessons learned that improve future health planning and interventions
options.B: It prevents community members from complaining to political leaders
options.C: It automatically secures a larger budget for the following year
options.D: It proves that nurses never make mistakes during fieldwork

explanation: Evaluating past successes and failures shows what works best, guiding better decisions for the next community health cycle. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h9)

question: Which Nigerian agency is well known for regulating food and drug safety?

options.A: JAMB
options.B: NAFDAC
options.C: NYSC
options.D: FRSC

explanation: NAFDAC (National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control) is our main regulatory body for food and drugs in Nigeria. Proudly Nigerian nursing knowledge!

question: What is the main goal of the Model for Improvement in healthcare?

options.A: To increase the total number of administrative reports filled out daily
options.B: To replace traditional nursing judgment with computer algorithms
options.C: To help clinical teams make practical changes that improve patient outcomes
options.D: To punish staff members who make mistakes during patient care

explanation: You got this! The model is simply a guide to help healthcare workers make meaningful, tested changes that make patient care better every day.

question: What key nursing action should you provide all through a teenager's labor?

options.A: Delayed monitoring of vital signs
options.B: Empathetic, continuous supportive presence
options.C: Restriction of all oral fluids
options.D: Complete physical isolation from family

explanation: Wonderful! Staying close, encouraging her, and offering a comforting presence helps lower fear and keeps her going strong.

question: Why is the eardrum (tympanic membrane) such a great spot to check core body temperature?

options.A: It shares a blood supply with the brain's temperature center
options.B: It is completely protected from any room air
options.C: Earwax never affects the reading
options.D: It always shows the highest temperature on the body

explanation: The eardrum shares blood vessels with the hypothalamus (your body's thermostat), giving you a very true picture of core temperature.

question: Which action by a nurse manager shows great stewardship of unit resources?

options.A: Ordering excess supplies just to make sure the budget is fully spent
options.B: Monitoring supply usage closely to prevent waste and expired stock
options.C: Refusing to participate in hospital financial planning meetings
options.D: Ignoring indirect costs because they cannot be traced to a single patient

explanation: Keeping an eye on inventory prevents waste and ensures your ward always has what it needs without throwing money away. You're thinking like a true nurse leader!

question: What is the main problem when the heart suddenly fails to pump properly?

options.A: An immediate and permanent increase in body temperature
options.B: Complete paralysis of the skeletal muscles in the lower limbs
options.C: Uncontrolled overproduction of red blood cells in the bone marrow
options.D: A dangerous drop in systemic blood pressure and oxygen delivery

explanation: If the heart pump slows or stops, pressure drops and oxygen stops reaching the tissues that need it most. Spotting this early saves lives!

question: How do long-acting injectable antipsychotics make community care easier?

options.A: They can be administered without any medical professional present
options.B: They completely eliminate all possible side effects of the medication
options.C: They remove the need for daily pill-taking and ensure steady medication levels
options.D: They cure the underlying genetic cause of the psychotic disorder

explanation: You're doing great! Injectables save patients from swallowing pills every single day and keep their drug levels nice and steady.

question: What is a common sign of compassion fatigue in disaster nurses?

options.A: Emotional numbness, irritability, and burnout
options.B: Increased energy and enthusiasm for work
options.C: Complete indifference to physical illnesses
options.D: An intense desire to work double shifts daily

explanation: Absorbing too much trauma without adequate recovery leads to emotional exhaustion and classic signs of burnout. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T6#GNS315_U5_T6_h8)

question: A nurse is caring for a patient with acute glomerulonephritis. Which nursing action is most critical during the acute phase?

options.A: Providing a high-protein diet to rebuild lost muscle
options.B: Massaging swollen legs to improve local circulation
options.C: Accurately measuring every intake and output volume
options.D: Encouraging high fluid intake by offering extra water

explanation: Tracking every drop that goes in and comes out (I&O) is essential to monitor failing kidney function and catch dangerous fluid buildup early.

question: Which patient is likely experiencing the highest compounded risk of healthcare disparities based on intersectionality?

options.A: A young male university student with private insurance
options.B: An impoverished elderly woman with a physical disability
options.C: A healthy adult woman living in an affluent neighborhood
options.D: A middle-aged man with a stable corporate job

explanation: This patient carries multiple intersecting vulnerabilities: gender, poverty, advanced age, and disability, which multiply barriers to care. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T22#GNS225_U5_T22_h6)

question: In secretory diarrhoea, why do patients lose water so quickly?

options.A: The liver fails to produce bile acids for digestion
options.B: Intestinal cells actively pump excessive water into the gut lumen
options.C: Stomach acid production increases to dangerous levels
options.D: The kidneys stop filtering waste products completely

explanation: Think of it like an open tap! Toxins trick the cells in the intestines into pushing out lots of water and salt into the gut faster than the body can absorb it.

question: A patient is staring blankly, speaking very little, and showing no emotion after an accident. What are they likely experiencing?

options.A: Aggressive hostility
options.B: Emotional numbness
options.C: Delusional psychosis
options.D: Hyper-arousal panic

explanation: Spot on! Right after trauma, a patient's mind can freeze up or go numb, making them look quiet, blank, and detached.

question: What is a common community-wide consequence when people witness widespread unsafe injection practices?

options.A: A sudden surplus of medical supply inventories
options.B: Immediate eradication of vector-borne illnesses
options.C: Increased funding for local nursing institutions
options.D: Erosion of public trust in legitimate health campaigns

explanation: When patients are terrified of catching a new disease at the clinic, they lose faith and stop coming back for essential immunizations and health care. Trust is fragile!

question: Which of these is a classic input device you might use while giving medications?

options.A: A bedside monitor screen
options.B: A laser printer
options.C: An emergency alarm speaker
options.D: A barcode scanner

explanation: Spot on! Input devices 'feed' information into the computer. Scanning a patient's wristband sends their details straight into the system.

question: What actually happens when a mast cell 'degranulates' during an allergy attack?

options.A: Antibodies are slowly manufactured inside the bone marrow
options.B: Inflammatory chemicals are rapidly released into the bloodstream
options.C: White blood cells consume and destroy the foreign trigger
options.D: Red blood cells multiply quickly to fight off the allergen

explanation: Mast cells act like tiny storage bags of histamine. When triggered, they pop open and dump their contents directly into your circulation, causing classic allergy symptoms.

question: What is the main benefit of placing a severe COVID-19 patient in the prone position (lying on their stomach)?

options.A: It improves oxygen exchange and lung expansion
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for intravenous lines
options.C: It prevents the patient from coughing during sleep
options.D: It allows the patient to feed themselves more easily

explanation: Well done! Gravity helps open up parts of the lungs that are pressed down when lying on the back, making it much easier for the patient to get oxygen.

question: Which grade of moulding describes skull bones that overlap firmly but can still be separated by finger pressure?

options.A: Grade 3 moulding
options.B: Grade 1 moulding
options.C: Grade 4 moulding
options.D: Grade 0 moulding

explanation: Grade 1 means the bones overlap slightly but remain reducible with gentle pressure. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T14#GNS121_U6_T14_h3)

question: A researcher gets a Cronbach's alpha of 0.82 for a new nursing burnout scale. What does this tell us?

options.A: The responses given by the patients are completely invalid
options.B: The questionnaire is unstable and changes too much over time
options.C: The questions on the scale measure completely different traits
options.D: The scale has strong internal consistency

explanation: Any alpha score above 0.70 is usually a green light showing your questions work well together as a team!

question: Why must nurses care about how medications are stored on the ward?

options.A: Pharmaceutical companies only trust nurses with liquid medications
options.B: Hospital pharmacists do not understand basic ward temperature needs
options.C: Nurses handle drugs from the supply point to actual bedside administration
options.D: The law requires nurses to manufacture all ward level supplies

explanation: Spot on! You are the crucial link between the pharmacy and the patient's bedside, making drug safety a key part of your daily care.

question: Why is building therapeutic rapport so important before starting a psychosocial assessment?

options.A: It guarantees the client will take all prescribed medications on time.
options.B: It stops the client from ever feeling sad about their illness.
options.C: It helps the client feel safe enough to share honest personal feelings.
options.D: It allows the nurse to skip asking about family medical history.

explanation: Trust allows clients to lower their guard and discuss sensitive emotional and mental health topics openly with the nurse. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T5#GNS222_U3_T5_h3)

question: Why should we worry when livestock farmers use antibiotics too frequently?

options.A: It causes animals to stop producing milk entirely
options.B: It can contribute to antimicrobial resistance
options.C: It turns the meat a bright green color
options.D: It makes the meat taste bitter to consumers

explanation: Overusing antibiotics on animals creates tougher, resistant germs that can eventually spread to humans and shrug off our best medications.

question: A patient's fasting blood sugar comes back at 115 mg/dL. How should you interpret this?

options.A: It confirms active type 1 diabetes
options.B: It is a completely normal result
options.C: It indicates prediabetes and impaired fasting glucose
options.D: It shows the patient had severe low blood sugar

explanation: Values between 100 and 125 mg/dL sit in the prediabetic zone. It's a great warning sign for patients to adjust their diet and lifestyle early!

question: How does a well-motivated nurse protect patient safety at the bedside?

options.A: By removing the need for doctors to write formal medication orders
options.B: By automatically doubling the nurse-to-patient staffing ratio
options.C: By increasing vigilance to catch subtle signs of clinical deterioration early
options.D: By speeding up the discharge process regardless of clinical status

explanation: When you are alert and motivated, you easily notice tiny changes in a patient's condition and can save the day early!

question: A grieving family arrives shortly after their relative passes away. What is the best thing to do?

options.A: Give them a detailed lecture on the stages of human grief
options.B: Instruct them to leave quickly so post-mortem care can begin
options.C: Ask them to sign discharge paperwork before entering the room
options.D: Provide a quiet space and allow them uninterrupted time with their loved one

explanation: You're doing great! Giving families private time helps them begin to process their loss peacefully.

question: What is the primary focus of a community diagnosis?

options.A: Treating individual patients in a hospital ward
options.B: Diagnosing rare diseases in laboratory animals
options.C: Inspecting the financial records of a local clinic
options.D: Assessing the health status and needs of an entire population

explanation: A community diagnosis looks at the whole population and its environment rather than focusing on a single sick person. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h1)

question: What is the main danger of leaving clear units of measurement off a bar chart's axis?

options.A: The hospital will fail to meet basic fire safety codes
options.B: The chart software will crash and delete the saved file
options.C: Patients will refuse to take their prescribed medications
options.D: Readers may misinterpret the data and make poor clinical decisions

explanation: Without clear units, nobody can tell if the numbers represent counts, percentages, or money. Always label your axes!

question: Why is pushing down on top of the mother's bump (fundal pressure) a big no-no during shoulder dystocia?

options.A: It stops the placenta from delivering after the baby
options.B: It makes the baby turn around into a breech position
options.C: It causes the mother's blood pressure to drop too low
options.D: It can cause the trapped shoulder to wedge tighter and rupture the uterus

explanation: Pushing from above only jams the shoulder harder against the bone. Avoid fundal pressure completely in shoulder dystocia!

question: What happens in a 'concealed' type of placental abruption?

options.A: The separation occurs entirely at the edge of the placental disk
options.B: Blood accumulates behind the placenta and does not escape outwardly
options.C: Blood flows rapidly through the cervix as bright red fluid
options.D: The placenta detaches silently without any pain or bleeding whatsoever

explanation: In a concealed abruption, blood gets trapped inside the uterus. This means external bleeding looks deceptively small while internal shock can develop quickly. Great job keeping this in mind!

question: When should standard infection control precautions be applied in a reproductive health clinic?

options.A: Exclusively during surgical childbirth procedures
options.B: Only when visitors are observing the clinical ward
options.C: To every single client regardless of infection status
options.D: Only when caring for patients with confirmed infections

explanation: Correct! Treat every patient's body fluids as potentially infectious. This keeps both you and the patients safe every single day.

question: In research, what do we mean when we say a tool is 'reliable'?

options.A: How easy the questionnaire is for elderly patients to read
options.B: How fast the researcher can collect data from patients
options.C: How consistently the tool produces the same results
options.D: Whether the tool measures what it is supposed to measure

explanation: Think of reliability like a dependable weighing scale—if you step on it five times in a row and get the exact same weight, it's reliable (even if it needs calibration later!). It's all about consistency.

question: Which factor is critical to maintain during the implementation of a health project?

options.A: Relying solely on commands from foreign experts
options.B: Excluding local leaders from daily operations
options.C: Strict secrecy about how funds and materials are spent
options.D: Transparency and clear communication among all participants

explanation: Open communication keeps everyone informed, builds trust, and prevents conflicts during project execution. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T5#GNS124_U4_T5_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of contact tracing during an infectious disease outbreak?

options.A: To punish patients who failed to report their symptoms early
options.B: To test new antibiotics on healthy community members
options.C: To disinfect all public water systems in the region
options.D: To identify individuals who may have been exposed to an infection source

explanation: Contact tracing is like detective work—we track down everyone who crossed paths with an infected person so we can protect and monitor them early.

question: What is the primary goal of the teach-back method during patient education?

options.A: To test the patient's ability to read complex medical textbooks
options.B: To prove that the nurse is an expert in pharmacology
options.C: To check if the patient truly understands their medication instructions
options.D: To make the nursing consultation take longer than necessary

explanation: The teach-back method requires the client to repeat instructions in their own words, confirming comprehension and revealing any remaining confusion. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T2#GNS215_U4_T2_h5)

question: What are the three core parts of the famous epidemiological triangle?

options.A: Source, vector, and cure
options.B: Bacteria, virus, and parasite
options.C: Agent, host, and environment
options.D: Infection, symptom, and recovery

explanation: Never forget the classic trio: the Agent (the germ), the Host (the person), and the Environment (the surroundings). You've got this memorized now!

question: Why do community nurses love using practical cooking demonstrations with local foods?

options.A: They allow the nurse to sell cooking utensils to rural women
options.B: They show caregivers how to prepare affordable, nutrient-dense meals using familiar ingredients
options.C: They replace the need for hospital-based medical treatments entirely
options.D: They prove that imported foreign foods are superior to local produce

explanation: Well done! Cooking demos turn nutrition tips into real-life kitchen skills using food that families can easily find and afford locally. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T7#GNS313_U3_T7_h7)

question: A client gets mild sedation to stay calm during a long MRI. What must the nurse watch most closely?

options.A: Breathing rate and oxygen levels
options.B: Bowel sounds in all four abdominal areas
options.C: The exact room temperature
options.D: How fast the client can walk afterward

explanation: Sedatives can slow down breathing, so keeping an eye on the patient's respiratory rate and oxygen is top priority!

question: Once Luteinizing Hormone (LH) finally reaches the gonads, what is its main job?

options.A: It lowers overall body temperature
options.B: It stimulates sex steroid production
options.C: It stops the secretion of GnRH
options.D: It triggers immediate linear height growth

explanation: Spot on! LH targets specific cells in the gonads to prompt the creation of powerhouse sex hormones like testosterone and estrogen.

question: During triage, a patient has severe head injuries, no pulse, and is not breathing even after opening the airway. What START category do they get?

options.A: Yellow
options.B: Black
options.C: Red
options.D: Green

explanation: Patients who have sadly passed away or have injuries incompatible with life are tagged black (expectant) so resources can go to those who can be saved.

question: What major problem in Nigerian healthcare do HMO payment systems try to solve?

options.A: Too many free drugs in public pharmacies
options.B: Excessive use of traditional herbal medicine
options.C: Heavy reliance on out-of-pocket spending
options.D: A shortage of medical textbooks in universities

explanation: Out-of-pocket spending forces families to pay cash immediately at the hospital, often leading to poverty or delayed care, which HMO prepayment prevents. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h2)

question: Which sign is a clinical indicator of severe respiratory distress in an adult patient?

options.A: Relaxed posture in a flat bed
options.B: Slow and deep regular breathing
options.C: Use of accessory neck muscles
options.D: Warm and pink skin coloration

explanation: When breathing becomes very hard, patients use their neck and chest muscles to help force air in and out. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h3)

question: What makes the foramen ovale snap shut at birth?

options.A: Higher pressure in the left atrium compared to the right atrium
options.B: The physical tie placed on the umbilical cord
options.C: Contraction of the heart muscle due to cold air
options.D: A sudden drop in the baby's core body temperature

explanation: As blood floods back from the newly working lungs into the left side of the heart, the pressure pushes the little flap of the foramen ovale shut. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h7)

question: During a clinic visit, a husband answers every question for his quiet wife, and she won't make eye contact. What should you suspect?

options.A: An imbalance in power and communication within the family
options.B: The hospital waiting room is curing her anxiety
options.C: The wife has perfect physical and mental health
options.D: The couple communicates like absolute experts

explanation: Pay attention to body language! When one person always speaks for another, it often points to a power imbalance or fear holding the quieter partner back.

question: A rural clinic notices a weekly increase in watery diarrhea during the rainy season. What should the nurses do first?

options.A: Ignore the data unless every single bed in the clinic is full
options.B: Close the clinic temporarily until the rainy season finishes
options.C: Wait until the end of the year to calculate annual averages
options.D: Report the trend upward to trigger quick public health support

explanation: Early reporting lets health authorities investigate water sources and rush supplies before things spiral into a full epidemic. You are thinking like a true public health nurse!

question: Why shouldn't you rely purely on personal opinion in a nursing paper?

options.A: Instructors simply do not like reading personal thoughts
options.B: Clinical claims must rest on verifiable evidence
options.C: Personal opinions are always grammatically incorrect
options.D: It takes too much time to write out opinions

explanation: Spot on! Nursing is an evidence-based field, meaning we always back our care with proven facts rather than just guesswork.

question: You previously referred a postpartum mother for family planning. During her baby's immunization visit, what should you do?

options.A: Assume she went and make no further mention of the referral
options.B: Scold her publicly for failing to attend the scheduled appointment
options.C: Resend the exact same referral letter without speaking to her
options.D: Ask the client if she successfully visited the family planning clinic

explanation: Following up during routine visits shows you care and helps ensure she gets the support she needs for her family goals.

question: A nurse supervisor spends the morning making duty rosters, checking medical supplies, and enforcing hospital rules. What role is she mostly showing?

options.A: Management
options.B: Advocacy
options.C: Leadership
options.D: Mentorship

explanation: Handling rosters, stock counts, and institutional rules are classic day-to-day management tasks. Spot on!

question: What CD4+ cell count threshold defines the progression from HIV infection to AIDS?

options.A: Below 50 cells per microliter
options.B: Below 200 cells per microliter
options.C: Below 500 cells per microliter
options.D: Below 1000 cells per microliter

explanation: Correct! Once the CD4+ count drops below 200 cells per microliter, the condition is classified as AIDS, indicating severe immune suppression.

question: Where should a completed incident report be submitted in the hospital?

options.A: Pinned to the public notice board in the main nursing station
options.B: Glued permanently inside the front cover of the patient's bedside chart
options.C: Mailed straight to the national nursing council office
options.D: Submitted directly to the quality or risk management department

explanation: That's right! Incident reports go straight to risk management or quality units, keeping them separate from the patient's clinical bedside chart.

question: Why do red blood cells take on a crescent or sickle shape in sickle cell anaemia?

options.A: Dehydration causes the bone marrow to manufacture flat instead of round cells
options.B: Excess iron in the bloodstream physically crushes the cells into sharp points
options.C: White blood cells attack the red blood cells and reshape their outer membranes
options.D: Abnormal haemoglobin molecules stick together to form rigid rods when oxygen is low

explanation: Think of it like a chain reaction: when oxygen drops, HbS molecules clump into stiff rods that push the cell into that classic crescent sickle shape.

question: Why is it important to know a germ's 'portal of exit' when caring for an infectious patient?

options.A: It calculates the total number of pathogens living inside the host.
options.B: It helps predict how the pathogen might leave the body to spread to others.
options.C: It determines the specific blood type compatibility of the host.
options.D: It reveals the exact genetic mutation rate of the invading organism.

explanation: Spot-on! Understanding the portal of exit shows you how germs leave the body (like through coughs or body fluids) so you can put up barriers and stop them.

question: Which of these is NOT part of routine family planning services?

options.A: Adolescent reproductive health education
options.B: Infertility management and counseling
options.C: Provision of modern contraceptive methods
options.D: Performing major abdominal surgeries

explanation: You got it! Family planning clinics focus on counseling, birth control, and fertility support—not major operations like removing an appendix.

question: If both parents have the sickle cell trait (AS), what is the chance they will have a child with sickle cell anaemia (SS)?

options.A: 100 percent
options.B: 25 percent
options.C: 50 percent
options.D: 75 percent

explanation: Genetics can be tricky, but with AS carriers, there's a 1 in 4 (25%) chance per pregnancy of having an SS child. Knowing this helps us counsel families better!

question: What is a common emotional response experienced by a person who has recently acquired a permanent physical disability?

options.A: Complete indifference toward their physical health status
options.B: Immediate and permanent acceptance of the new lifestyle
options.C: Euphoria over lifestyle changes and reduced responsibilities
options.D: Grief and a process similar to mourning a loss

explanation: Patients frequently experience a grief reaction as they process the loss of their previous physical abilities and independence. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T9#GNS225_U5_T9_h6)

question: If someone has a family history of anxiety, what role does a major life stressor play?

options.A: It only affects physical heart rate and blood pressure
options.B: It can act as a trigger that activates the underlying condition
options.C: It completely erases any chance of developing symptoms
options.D: It replaces the need for biological evaluation entirely

explanation: Think of the genetic tendency as a loaded gun, and severe stress as the trigger that pulls it.

question: Why should nurses use open-ended questions when talking to a child about an injury?

options.A: To avoid leading the child and contaminating potential legal evidence
options.B: To speed up the clinical assessment process during busy shifts
options.C: To comply with hospital billing guidelines for pediatric trauma
options.D: To encourage the child to blame their siblings instead of parents

explanation: Asking leading questions puts words in the child's mouth, which ruins the reliability of any future legal investigation.

question: What is meant by a disease 'reservoir'?

options.A: Where the infectious agent normally lives and multiplies
options.B: The Department of Health data storage unit
options.C: A device used to measure patient body temperature
options.D: The specific medication given to kill a virus

explanation: Correct! A reservoir is the natural hiding and breeding place—whether in humans, animals, or soil—where a germ thrives and reproduces.

question: Why should medical equipment like stethoscopes be kept inside an isolation patient's room?

options.A: Because isolation rooms have extra storage space
options.B: To stop equipment from getting stolen by visitors
options.C: To save nursing time on cleaning stethoscopes
options.D: To prevent carrying germs out on shared equipment to other patients

explanation: Using dedicated equipment inside the room stops the stethoscope or blood pressure cuff from acting as a vehicle that spreads infection to the next room. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h6)

question: What ethical action must nurse researchers take if an intervention being tested in a prospective trial proves to be significantly harmful?

options.A: Ask participants to sign a waiver accepting the new dangers
options.B: Hide the adverse results until the final academic paper is published
options.C: Continue the trial until the originally scheduled end date anyway
options.D: Stop the trial immediately to protect participants from further harm

explanation: Researcher safety oversight demands that patient welfare always supersedes study completion if unexpected dangers emerge. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T15#GNS224_U1_T15_h6)

question: Which of the following is an example of primary data collection?

options.A: Reviewing old hospital admission registers in the record room
options.B: Conducting house-to-house surveys and interviews with residents
options.C: Reading national census reports published ten years ago
options.D: Downloading international World Health Organization PDF reports

explanation: Primary data is gathered directly from the source by the healthcare worker conducting the investigation. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h3)

question: A Nigerian nurse wants to help reduce maternal mortality in a rural community. What is the best first step?

options.A: Tell the villagers to stop using traditional birth attendants without offering alternatives
options.B: Wait for international organizations to solve the problem without local data
options.C: Import expensive foreign medical equipment that the local clinic cannot power
options.D: Conduct a local study to identify specific barriers preventing women from seeking antenatal care

explanation: Spot on! Local research helps us uncover the real root causes of a problem so we can design solutions that truly fit the community.

question: Which of the following best describes the multi-faceted role of a nurse working in a Nigerian primary health center?

options.A: Acting as a clinician, educator, manager, and community advocate
options.B: Writing laws and policies for the federal parliament
options.C: Performing complex heart surgeries in a private luxury suite
options.D: Working strictly as an accountant in a corporate bank office

explanation: PHC nurses handle diverse responsibilities, from treating patients and teaching families to managing clinic supplies and leading community health outreach. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h10)

question: Why is communication different in a community setting compared to a busy hospital ward?

options.A: Community nurses only use written notes instead of talking
options.B: Hospital patients never need verbal health instructions
options.C: Hospital care relies entirely on non-verbal body signs
options.D: Community nurses build long-term relationships with families

explanation: Because community nurses work closely with the same neighborhoods and families over time, their communication focuses heavily on long-term relationships and prevention. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h1)

question: Why should a nurse focus on health problems that residents care about the most?

options.A: It saves the hospital from spending any money on medical supplies
options.B: Residents are more motivated to participate when the project matches their interests
options.C: Government regulations legally force citizens to attend health meetings
options.D: It guarantees that no one in the village will ever fall sick again

explanation: When people see you addressing a problem they actually care about, they will gladly join in and help!

question: How do intestinal parasite eggs most commonly spread to people?

options.A: Mosquito vector bites
options.B: The fecal-oral route
options.C: Direct airborne droplets
options.D: Unprotected skin contact

explanation: Most gut parasites spread when tiny amounts of contaminated matter reach the mouth via unwashed hands, food, or water. Good to know for patient education!

question: Why do nurses need to understand workplace hazards?

options.A: To calculate company profits
options.B: To diagnose every non-work illness in the community
options.C: To help prevent both sudden injuries and long-term illnesses
options.D: To replace the factory safety manager

explanation: As nurses, knowing about workplace hazards helps us protect workers, advocate for their safety, and stop health issues before they even start!

question: What does a Barcode Medication Administration (BCMA) system help you check before giving drugs to a patient?

options.A: The insurance coverage approval status for the specific prescription
options.B: The current market cost of the prescribed pharmaceutical drug
options.C: The correct matching of the nurse, client, and medication package
options.D: The exact manufacturing date of the syringe or intravenous tubing

explanation: BCMA scanners are great tools. They scan your badge, the patient's wristband, and the drug packet to make sure it's the right drug for the right person! [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h4)

question: What right does every participant have during a clinical research experiment?

options.A: To change the research questions whenever they want
options.B: To receive free lifetime medical care after the study
options.C: To choose which group they want to be placed in
options.D: To withdraw from the study at any time without penalty

explanation: Participation is completely voluntary, and patients can quit whenever they choose without affecting their regular hospital treatment. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T7#GNS224_U1_T7_h7)

question: What is the primary goal of homeostasis in the human body?

options.A: Maintaining a stable internal environment
options.B: Speeding up cellular reproduction
options.C: Increasing muscle mass during exercise
options.D: Preventing all exposure to external bacteria

explanation: Homeostasis keeps vital internal conditions like temperature, blood pressure, and chemical balance within a safe, stable range. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h6)

question: A 14-year-old girl is growing fast and has started her monthly periods. How does this affect her food and nutrient needs?

options.A: She only needs extra water and no other dietary changes
options.B: Her nutritional demands decrease because her body is slowing down
options.C: Her nutritional demands remain exactly the same as childhood
options.D: Her nutritional demands increase significantly to support growth and blood loss

explanation: Exactly! Rapid body growth plus monthly blood loss means she needs more energy, protein, and key minerals to stay strong and healthy.

question: What is the main goal of nursing care for a dying patient?

options.A: Forcing the patient through all five stages of grief
options.B: Maximizing comfort, dignity, and holistic support
options.C: Finding a miracle cure for the disease
options.D: Restricting visitors to keep the room quiet

explanation: At the end of life, our main duty as nurses is palliative care: keeping them comfortable, pain-free, and deeply respected.

question: What is the most common reason clients stop using their family planning supply method?

options.A: They achieve permanent sterilization immediately
options.B: Fear or experience of bothersome side effects
options.C: The method is always 100 percent free of charge
options.D: Lack of interest from their healthcare provider

explanation: Minor things like spotting or weight changes can scare clients if they aren't warned ahead of time. Pre-counseling makes all the difference!

question: Why does wearing the correct glove size matter so much in clinical work?

options.A: It prevents tearing and keeps your fingers nimble
options.B: It stops the material from causing latex allergies
options.C: It keeps the gloves completely sterile
options.D: It means you don't have to wash your hands afterwards

explanation: Gloves that are too tight will easily rip, while oversized gloves make it hard to grip things. Finding your right size is key!

question: What is the main goal of teaching a community about choking prevention?

options.A: To eliminate the sale of all round food items in local grocery stores
options.B: To ensure families purchase expensive medical safety equipment
options.C: To train every citizen to perform complex surgical procedures at home
options.D: To empower caregivers with knowledge to prevent incidents before they occur

explanation: Exactly! Teaching families how to spot risks and fix food shapes helps stop emergencies before they even start. Prevention is our best tool!

question: In which situation should a routine paracentesis definitely NOT be done?

options.A: A history of controlled high blood pressure
options.B: Mild swelling in both ankles and feet
options.C: A slight elevation in liver enzymes
options.D: An acute surgical abdomen needing immediate operation

explanation: If a patient needs emergency surgery for an acute belly issue, a routine fluid tap is not appropriate.

question: Why is continuous heart monitoring a must right after a successful defibrillation?

options.A: To ensure the patient stays awake during recovery
options.B: To verify that the defibrillator battery is still fully charged
options.C: To measure the exact electrical resistance of the skin
options.D: To catch early warning signs of recurrent arrhythmias or re-arrest

explanation: Just because the heart restarted doesn't mean they're out of the woods. These patients are very fragile and can easily slip right back into a dangerous rhythm.

question: Why is the first week or two after hospital discharge considered a critical time for surgical recovery patients?

options.A: Because patients are usually unconscious for the entire first week
options.B: Because hospital staff move in to live with the patient permanently
options.C: Because all wound stitches dissolve within the first twenty-four hours
options.D: Because the risk of surgical site infection remains high during this period

explanation: Wounds are still healing and vulnerable shortly after surgery, making vigilant home monitoring essential. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T8#GNS324_U1_T8_h3)

question: What is the main difference between decorticate and decerebrate posturing when scoring motor response?

options.A: Decorticate involves abnormal flexion inward, while decerebrate involves rigid extension outward
options.B: Decorticate affects only the legs, while decerebrate affects only the arms
options.C: Decorticate is scored as a 5, while decerebrate is scored as a 4
options.D: Decorticate means the patient obeys commands, while decerebrate means they make no sound

explanation: Think of decorticate (flexion/inward toward the core) scoring a 3, and decerebrate (extension/rigid outward) scoring a 2. Both point to serious brain stress, but knowing the physical posturing helps you chart accurately.

question: Which lethal heart rhythm requires immediate defibrillation and emergency response?

options.A: First-degree heart block
options.B: Sinus bradycardia
options.C: Premature atrial contractions
options.D: Ventricular fibrillation

explanation: Ventricular fibrillation is a chaotic heart rhythm where the ventricles quiver instead of pumping blood, causing cardiac arrest that requires immediate electrical shock. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T13#GNS213_U1_T13_h4)

question: A patient arrives at a primary health clinic with a severe postpartum hemorrhage that requires a blood transfusion. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Send the patient home with oral pain relievers
options.B: Stabilize the patient and quickly arrange transfer to a CEmONC facility
options.C: Perform a major surgical operation right there in the primary clinic
options.D: Wait for the bleeding to stop on its own before taking action

explanation: Basic clinics cannot handle blood transfusions or major surgery, so quick stabilization and emergency referral are mandatory. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T44#GNS214_U1_T44_h5)

question: What is the main danger when a nurse transcribes (copies) a medication order?

options.A: It removes the need for nurses to check patient identity
options.B: It makes doctors write prescriptions much slower than usual
options.C: It permanently deletes previous medication history from the chart
options.D: It introduces opportunities for human error and misinterpretation

explanation: Spot on! Every time an order is manually copied over, there's a risk that numbers, decimals, or abbreviations might be misread.

question: How long does a released egg typically survive after ovulation if it doesn't meet a sperm?

options.A: 48 to 72 hours
options.B: 12 to 24 hours
options.C: 3 to 5 days
options.D: 1 week

explanation: An unfertilized egg has a surprisingly short lifespan! Once it leaves the ovary, it's only viable for about half a day to a full day.

question: What are vulval varicose veins?

options.A: Benign fluid-filled cysts inside the myometrium of the uterus
options.B: Infections of the Bartholin glands located near the vaginal opening
options.C: Inflammation of the urinary bladder lining caused by bacteria
options.D: Enlarged and dilated blood vessels on the external genitalia

explanation: Spotting swollen, twisted veins on the labia or external parts can look scary, but they are just like varicose veins on the legs—they are simply enlarged blood vessels. You've got this!

question: How is the care for a stable patient with a bruised heart (contusion) different from someone with a bleeding heart wound?

options.A: The blunt injury patient requires immediate open-heart surgery every time.
options.B: The blunt injury patient often receives monitoring and supportive care instead of immediate surgery.
options.C: Medical management is never used for any form of chest trauma.
options.D: Penetrating injuries are always treated with rest and pain medication alone.

explanation: If a patient is stable with a bruised heart, we usually watch them closely in the ICU. But an active stab or gunshot wound? That needs immediate surgery!

question: During a massive disaster with limited supplies, how should medical items be shared out?

options.A: Exclusively to patients who arrived first at the emergency department
options.B: Based on objective survival criteria rather than arrival time
options.C: Based on the patient's personal wealth and social status
options.D: Randomly distributed using a lottery system among all injured

explanation: Spot on! We focus on saving the most lives by giving resources to those with the best chance of survival, rather than just who arrived first.

question: Who among the following is NOT typically part of the healthcare team managing essential drugs?

options.A: Medical doctor
options.B: Clinical pharmacist
options.C: International airline pilot
options.D: Registered nurse

explanation: Easy one! Pilots fly planes, while doctors, nurses, and pharmacists work together to manage patient medications.

question: As a nursing student, why is it helpful to know different research categories?

options.A: To write prescriptions for patients independently
options.B: To diagnose complex diseases without a doctor
options.C: To replace hands-on clinical ward practice
options.D: To decide if a study can guide safe patient care

explanation: Spot on! Knowing research categories helps you evaluate evidence so you can confidently apply safe, proven ideas when caring for your patients. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T4#GNS217_U1_T4_h1)

question: What does the letter 'S' stand for in the MIST handover acronym used during transport?

options.A: Special bed requests
options.B: Surgical history notes
options.C: Staff names on duty
options.D: Signs and vital numbers

explanation: In the MIST format, S refers to the patient's vital signs and clinical observations noted during the journey. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T9#GNS315_U3_T9_h7)

question: What do we call the natural home where germs live, grow, and multiply?

options.A: Portal of exit
options.B: Susceptible host
options.C: Vector
options.D: Reservoir

explanation: Spot on! A reservoir can be a human, animal, plant, or soil where germs hang out and multiply.

question: What is the correct tool to measure the length of a 14-month-old child?

options.A: A flexible cloth tape measure
options.B: A vertical wall stadiometer
options.C: A hanging spring balance scale
options.D: An infantometer for recumbent length

explanation: Kids under two can't stand straight yet, so we use a flat measuring board (infantometer) while they lie down.

question: What is the main feature of Type III FGM?

options.A: Removal of only the clitoral prepuce
options.B: Piercing of the labia majora with metal rings
options.C: Creation of a covering seal that narrows the vaginal opening
options.D: Cauterization of the inner vaginal lining with heat

explanation: Correct! Type III (infibulation) involves cutting and joining the labia to form a seal, leaving only a very small opening for urine and menstrual flow.

question: When does continuous monitoring of a community mobilisation project take place?

options.A: Before entering the community for the first time
options.B: Throughout the implementation of the project
options.C: Only ten years after the project has ended
options.D: Never, because monitoring is unnecessary

explanation: Monitoring is an ongoing activity that happens while the project is running to ensure everything stays on track. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T2#GNS124_U4_T2_h7)

question: Why does unequal household power make it harder for some women to get healthcare?

options.A: It forces female patients to work in hazardous industrial environments
options.B: It automatically increases the physiological risk of contracting infectious diseases
options.C: It prevents women from independently seeking or funding their own medical care
options.D: It stops hospitals from hiring female doctors and nurses

explanation: If a woman has no control over household money and needs permission just to leave the house, getting to a clinic when she's sick becomes a massive hurdle.

question: What is the best and simplest guide for a nursing mother on how much fluid to drink?

options.A: Drink fluids whenever she feels thirsty
options.B: Avoid all liquids for two hours after each feeding
options.C: Drink only carbonated soft drinks to stay energized
options.D: Force herself to drink ten liters daily regardless of thirst

explanation: Your body's natural thirst cue is a fantastic guide during lactation. Drinking a glass of water during each nursing session is a wonderful habit to build.

question: What is the name of the special fund in Nigeria set up to directly support primary healthcare facilities?

options.A: Basic Health Care Provision Fund
options.B: Universal Health Infrastructure Grant
options.C: National Emergency Medical Reserve Fund
options.D: Federal Drug Procurement Account

explanation: The Basic Health Care Provision Fund (BHCPF) is designed precisely to boost primary healthcare delivery right down to the grassroots in Nigeria.

question: As a nurse, you'll hear about SBAR. What does this acronym stand for?

options.A: Shift, Bed, Analysis, Report
options.B: System, Blood, Assessment, Reaction
options.C: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation
options.D: Safety, Basic, Action, Review

explanation: Spot on! SBAR is your best friend for quick, clear handovers and phone calls with doctors. It helps you state the Situation, give the Background, share your Assessment, and state your Recommendation.

question: What is the typical duration of an occasional leave?

options.A: Exactly one hour under armed guard
options.B: An indefinite period until final discharge
options.C: A minimum of six consecutive months
options.D: A few hours to a couple of days

explanation: Occasional leave is short and sweet—just a few hours or a weekend break away from the ward environment.

question: Which of these is the most common and controllable risk factor for having a stroke?

options.A: Male gender
options.B: Advanced age
options.C: Genetic history
options.D: Hypertension

explanation: Correct! High blood pressure puts constant, dangerous strain on the brain's blood vessels, making it the number one risk factor we can manage.

question: What happens to a blood pressure reading if the cuff used on the patient's arm is too small?

options.A: It remains completely normal
options.B: It reads falsely high
options.C: It reads falsely low
options.D: It drops to zero

explanation: A cuff that is too small requires more pressure to compress the artery, resulting in an artificially elevated reading. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T16#GNS324_U4_T16_h3)

question: What is the main reason we use the ABCDEF protocol in emergency care?

options.A: To document nursing care for legal cover
options.B: To figure out the final medical diagnosis
options.C: To replace the need for lab tests
options.D: To find and treat life-threatening problems step-by-step

explanation: You've got this! The ABCDEF guide helps healthcare teams tackle the scariest, most immediate life threats first so nothing gets missed. Great job thinking like an emergency nurse!

question: Why are Class IV drugs effective for treating supraventricular tachycardia?

options.A: They completely eliminate all electrical activity in the heart wall
options.B: They speed up the natural pacemaker cells in the right atrium
options.C: They slow down conduction through the atrioventricular node
options.D: They force the ventricles to beat faster than the upper chambers

explanation: By slowing AV node conduction, these drugs break the rapid loop causing supraventricular tachycardia. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h6)

question: What is the name for that blood-tinged mucus plug that drops when the cervix starts opening up?

options.A: The show
options.B: Lightening
options.C: Bloody discharge
options.D: Amniotic fluid

explanation: We call it 'the show'! It's a classic early sign that the cervix is getting ready and opening up for labour.

question: What is a key requirement for a temporary health care waste storage room?

options.A: It must be located right inside the patient ward
options.B: It must be locked and secured against unauthorized access
options.C: It must have large glass windows for sunlight
options.D: It must be kept at freezing temperatures

explanation: Storage areas hold dangerous infectious or toxic materials and must remain locked to keep patients, visitors, and scavengers safe. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h6)

question: What makes a disaster different from a normal medical emergency?

options.A: An emergency never requires outside assistance.
options.B: A disaster affects only one patient at a time.
options.C: An emergency only happens inside a hospital building.
options.D: A disaster overwhelms local resources and community systems.

explanation: You've got this! A disaster is so big that it exhausts local clinics, hospitals, and supplies, meaning extra help from regional or national levels is needed.

question: What is your very first nursing action if an abdominal wound suddenly pops open and organs are exposed?

options.A: Cover the organs with sterile saline-soaked dressings and call the surgeon.
options.B: Use your gloved fingers to push the organs back inside.
options.C: Wrap a tight binder around the belly to squeeze the organs back in.
options.D: Leave the wound completely open to the fresh air.

explanation: Keep those exposed organs moist with sterile saline gauze so they don't dry out while you call for emergency surgical help. Emergency handled like a champ!

question: Why shouldn't a nurse rush in and do everything for a slow-moving rehab patient?

options.A: It prevents the client from ever needing assistive devices
options.B: It saves nursing time during busy morning shifts
options.C: Doing it for them reduces their chance to practice and slows down their independence
options.D: Hospital policies strictly forbid nurses from helping with dressing

explanation: It's tough to watch them struggle, but letting them do it themselves builds muscle memory and true independence. Patience is a nurse's superpower!

question: Why is it so important for nurses to directly ask new mothers about leakage or pain during postnatal visits?

options.A: Hospital policy requires a written confession of any weakness
options.B: Postnatal hormones cause temporary memory loss regarding physical symptoms
options.C: Midwives are legally forbidden from physical examinations without questions first
options.D: Patients often feel embarrassed to bring up issues like leakage or pain on their own

explanation: Spot on! Many women suffer quietly because they think postpartum leaking is just 'normal now'. As nurses, we must gently check in on them.

question: Where should used hypodermic needles and scalpel blades be disposed of immediately after use?

options.A: Black domestic waste bins
options.B: Puncture-resistant safety boxes
options.C: Cardboard packaging boxes
options.D: Open plastic wash basins

explanation: Sharps must always go into dedicated, puncture-proof safety containers to prevent accidental needle-stick injuries. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h8)

question: What does a categorical diagnostic approach assume about a client?

options.A: Every patient shares the exact same underlying brain chemistry
options.B: A person either has a specific disorder or does not
options.C: All psychological symptoms exist on an infinite sliding scale
options.D: Diagnosis should change daily based on mood

explanation: The categorical model views mental health conditions like a box: you either meet the criteria and have the diagnosis, or you don't.

question: What is the main goal of restorative nursing care in an SNF?

options.A: To reinforce therapy goals during everyday routine activities
options.B: To administer complex intravenous medications overnight
options.C: To replace formal physical therapy sessions entirely
options.D: To manage facility financial records and insurance claims

explanation: Restorative nursing helps residents practice their therapy skills during daily routines so they can hold onto their independence.

question: As a nurse caring for a yellow fever patient, which action is most critical to prioritize?

options.A: Administering routine oral iron supplements
options.B: Monitoring strict fluid intake and output
options.C: Encouraging high ambulation in the hallways
options.D: Applying cold water packs to the skin continuously

explanation: Brilliant! Because kidney failure can sneak up fast, tracking what goes in and out helps you catch trouble early. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T9#GNS214_U1_T9_h5)

question: What is the traditional foundation for caring for the sick and elderly in Nigerian society?

options.A: Missionary parish health outposts
options.B: The extended family system
options.C: State-run geriatric nursing homes
options.D: Private commercial health agencies

explanation: In our culture, we lean heavily on extended family members to look after and support older or sick relatives at home. Beautiful tradition!

question: What happens when a patient with a weak pancreas eats a heavy, fatty meal?

options.A: All excess fat is stored safely in the liver.
options.B: Unabsorbed fats pass through, causing oily stools and cramping.
options.C: The stomach completely stops all digestion permanently.
options.D: Fats instantly convert into muscle tissue.

explanation: Without enough pancreatic enzymes to break it down, fat passes right through the gut, leading to uncomfortable cramps and oily stools (steatorrhea).

question: Which tool do event managers commonly use to watch crowd movement and density in real time?

options.A: Post-event questionnaires
options.B: Weekly weather forecasts
options.C: Closed-circuit television cameras
options.D: Paper registration logs

explanation: CCTV camera feeds give security and medical teams 'eyes everywhere' so they can spot crowd build-ups instantly.

question: What must you check before giving a patient water after an upper GI scope?

options.A: That the patient's gag reflex has fully returned
options.B: That the patient's blood pressure is above normal
options.C: That the doctor has reviewed all laboratory results
options.D: That the patient has passed normal flatus

explanation: Their throat is usually numbed during the test. Checking for the gag reflex ensures they won't choke when they finally take a sip of water!

question: What is the main purpose of medication reconciliation in clinical practice?

options.A: To report pharmaceutical companies for high drug prices
options.B: To compare current medication orders against what the patient actually needs
options.C: To destroy expired medications found in the patient bedside locker
options.D: To calculate the total monthly cost of all prescribed drugs

explanation: Medication reconciliation is like a safety net! It helps catch missing medications that should be part of the patient's treatment plan.

question: What is the main job of nitric oxide when a man gets an erection?

options.A: Stimulating the sympathetic nervous system to contract the prostate
options.B: Relaxing smooth muscle to allow blood to fill the corpora cavernosa
options.C: Constricting local arteries to trap blood inside the pelvic cavity
options.D: Destroying excess fibrous tissue within the tunica albuginea

explanation: Nitric oxide acts like a smooth muscle relaxant in the blood vessels, letting blood rush in and fill the chambers (corpora cavernosa) to create firmness.

question: Why is the hospital incident report kept separate from the patient's main medical chart?

options.A: It serves as the primary legal bill sent to the health insurance
options.B: It is used internally for quality improvement and risk management
options.C: It proves that no mistake ever happened during the shift
options.D: It allows the patient to edit the nursing notes at home

explanation: Incident reports are special internal tools. They help the hospital track safety trends and fix systems, rather than acting as patient records.

question: What do we call large cells with multiple nuclei formed when virus-infected cells fuse together?

options.A: Neutrophils
options.B: Granulomas
options.C: Syncytia
options.D: Abscesses

explanation: Syncytia are giant multi-nucleated cells created when certain clever viruses trick neighboring cell membranes into melting together.

question: When checking blood tests for primary hypothyroidism, which result do you expect to see?

options.A: Decreased serum thyrotropin-releasing hormone
options.B: Decreased serum thyroid-stimulating hormone
options.C: Elevated serum thyroxine levels
options.D: Elevated serum thyroid-stimulating hormone

explanation: Think of the pituitary gland as a boss trying to get a lazy thyroid to work. When the thyroid slows down, the boss shouts louder by pumping out extra TSH! So a high TSH level is the main clue for primary hypothyroidism.

question: Why do geriatric facilities regularly conduct quality improvement audits?

options.A: To increase the cost of care for incoming residents
options.B: To eliminate the need for any government oversight
options.C: To ensure care practices remain safe, compassionate, and evidence-based
options.D: To find reasons to dismiss hardworking nursing staff

explanation: Audits help catch gaps in care early, prevent mistakes, and keep the environment safe and comforting for every resident. You're doing brilliantly!

question: Why is being sharp with clinical assessments extra important for a midwife working in a home setting?

options.A: Hospital policies dictate every step of home interventions
options.B: Advanced surgical equipment is always readily available
options.C: Clients at home never experience sudden medical complications
options.D: The midwife must rely on independent skills without immediate backup

explanation: When you are out in the field doing a home birth, there is no doctor or emergency trolley around the corner. Your own assessment skills are the first line of defense!

question: A patient catches a cold after touching a bedside table that hasn't been cleaned. What kind of transmission is this?

options.A: Droplet transmission
options.B: Airborne transmission
options.C: Indirect contact
options.D: Vector-borne transmission

explanation: Well done! Because the patient touched an object (a fomite) instead of the sick person directly, it's indirect contact.

question: Why are malnourished individuals much more vulnerable to severe infections?

options.A: Their immune systems lack the proper nutrients to mount a strong defense
options.B: Pathogens are naturally attracted to low protein levels in the blood
options.C: Stomach acid becomes too weak to kill ingested bacteria
options.D: Malnutrition stops white blood cells from circulating through the veins

explanation: Good nutrition is the fuel for immunity. Without the right nutrients, the body simply doesn't have the building blocks to fight off sickness effectively.

question: Which helpful cell in the central nervous system acts like a little garbage collector, clearing away germs and dead tissue?

options.A: Ependymal cells
options.B: Astrocytes
options.C: Microglia
options.D: Oligodendrocytes

explanation: Microglia are the immune defenders of the central nervous system. They clean up debris and fight off any unwanted invaders.

question: Which of these is a physical sign of grief that a patient might feel in their body?

options.A: Anger towards hospital staff
options.B: Social withdrawal
options.C: Tightness in the chest
options.D: Keeping a room untouched

explanation: Grief isn't just emotional—it can hurt physically too! Things like chest tightness, constant fatigue, and upset stomach are very real physical signs.

question: Why does an HMO require a formal referral before a patient sees a specialist?

options.A: To give the patient something to do on weekends
options.B: To make it as difficult as possible for sick people to get help
options.C: To ensure the specialist hospital gets less money from the pool
options.D: To control costs and ensure patients see the right expert for their condition

explanation: Gatekeeping prevents patients from bypassing basic clinics for expensive specialist care they might not actually need. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h4)

question: Why is the traditional mechanical approach to giving medications no longer enough?

options.A: It requires doctors to write more prescriptions
options.B: It prevents nurses from charting on computers
options.C: It ignores the patient's personal routine and individual needs
options.D: It takes too much time during a busy hospital shift

explanation: Simply handing over pills without considering the person's life often leads to poor adherence and missed doses. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T3#GNS125_U3_T3_h1)

question: What is the best way to count a patient's respiratory rate accurately without making them change how they breathe?

options.A: Announce loudly that you are starting to count breaths now
options.B: Count respirations discreetly right after taking the radial pulse without moving your hand away
options.C: Place a heavy hand on their chest to feel every rib movement
options.D: Ask them to take ten deep breaths so you can time it

explanation: Smart nursing! Patients often change their breathing if they know you're watching. Transitioning straight from the pulse keeps their breathing natural.

question: What is the scientific term used for parasitic worms in medical practice?

options.A: Bacteroids
options.B: Protozoa
options.C: Helminths
options.D: Mycoses

explanation: Helminths is the broad biological term used to describe parasitic worms that infect humans and animals. [learn more](GST114_U3_T6#GST114_U3_T6_h1)

question: A toddler is brought to the clinic with sunken eyes, fussiness, and drinks the ORS eagerly. How would you classify this dehydration?

options.A: Chronic malnutrition
options.B: Severe dehydration
options.C: Some dehydration
options.D: No dehydration

explanation: You got it! Irritability, sunken eyes, and drinking eagerly are classic signs of moderate ('some') dehydration. Giving ORS right here in the clinic will help them bounce back.

question: What is usually the very first step public health teams take when investigating a suspected disease outbreak?

options.A: Hold a press conference on national television
options.B: Close down all schools and markets in the entire country
options.C: Burn medical waste to destroy any remaining bacteria
options.D: Verify the diagnosis and confirm that an outbreak actually exists

explanation: Correct! Before launching a full investigation, health workers must make sure laboratory results and case numbers truly point to an outbreak.

question: What does 'asynchronous development' mean when talking about gifted children?

options.A: Language skills develop long before motor skills.
options.B: Physical growth happens much slower than in normal peers.
options.C: Intellectual, emotional, and physical ages do not match.
options.D: Emotional maturity always outpaces cognitive ability.

explanation: Exactly! Asynchronous just means uneven development. A child might have the mind of a 10-year-old, the emotions of a 6-year-old, and the body of an 8-year-old all at once. You're crushing this!

question: Which type of immunity is present right from birth and gives us quick, general protection?

options.A: Passive immunity
options.B: Adaptive immunity
options.C: Innate immunity
options.D: Artificial immunity

explanation: Innate immunity is your built-in armor! You are born with it, and it acts immediately whenever any foreign germ tries to sneak in, without needing any prior practice.

question: What does the letter 'M' stand for in the SMART criteria for objective formulation?

options.A: Moderate
options.B: Manageable
options.C: Mandatory
options.D: Measurable

explanation: In SMART planning, objectives must be measurable so the team can prove whether they achieved them or not. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h4)

question: Which behavioral change do we most often see in young children after experiencing a traumatic emergency?

options.A: Sudden independence and refusal of adult comfort
options.B: Complete emotional stability and mature coping
options.C: Advanced philosophical discussions about mortality
options.D: Behavioral regression like clinginess or bedwetting

explanation: Correct! Because little ones can't always put big stress into words, they often slide back to younger behaviors (regression) like clinging or bedwetting.

question: You walk past some open gutters filled with stagnant water near residential houses. What major health risk does this environment create?

options.A: Higher rates of chronic respiratory illnesses due to indoor smoke
options.B: Immediate outbreaks of genetic disorders among newborn infants
options.C: Widespread nutritional deficiencies from lack of agricultural soil
options.D: Increased breeding grounds for vectors like mosquitoes spreading malaria

explanation: Exactly! Stagnant water is basically a five-star hotel for mosquitoes, which makes malaria a huge risk for families nearby.

question: Before giving another dose of magnesium sulfate, which clinical sign must you check first?

options.A: Level of blood glucose
options.B: Size of the liver and spleen
options.C: Presence of knee-jerk patellar reflexes
options.D: Fetal heart rate variability

explanation: Awesome job! Losing the knee-jerk reflex is an early warning sign that magnesium is building up too much in the body, well before breathing slows down.

question: What does 'participatory governance' mean in primary health care?

options.A: Leaving all health decisions entirely to elected politicians
options.B: Allowing only doctors to vote on clinic budgets
options.C: Involving local community members in health planning and decisions
options.D: Handing over total hospital ownership to private investors

explanation: Spot on! Participatory governance means the community isn't just a receiver of care—they help shape the health services they get. Keep up the great work!

question: In public health nursing, how do we best describe a 'community'?

options.A: Any group of patients admitted to the same hospital ward
options.B: An individual family living in a single household
options.C: A group of people sharing social ties and common interests
options.D: A collection of medical doctors working in a clinic

explanation: Great job! A community is all about connection—shared ties, interactions, and a sense of belonging, rather than just being in a hospital building.

question: A nurse uses the hospital computer to check the medical chart of a famous musician admitted to a different ward, simply out of personal curiosity. What is the legal and ethical status of this action?

options.A: It is allowed if the nurse is off-duty during the chart review
options.B: It is acceptable as long as the nurse does not tell anyone else
options.C: It is a serious privacy breach because the nurse is outside the circle of care
options.D: It is encouraged so staff can offer collective words of encouragement

explanation: Looking at charts without a direct professional need for patient care violates data privacy laws and ethics. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h3)

question: A patient with uncontrolled chronic hypertension undergoes an ophthalmoscopy. Which finding is the nurse most likely to see documented?

options.A: A completely absent red reflex caused by a dense corneal scar
options.B: Total detachment of the sensory retina away from the back wall
options.C: Bright green pigment spots scattered evenly across the macula
options.D: Arteriovenous nicking where thickened arteries cross retinal veins

explanation: Chronic high blood pressure causes thickening and stiffening of retinal arterioles, leading to the classic sign of arteriovenous nicking. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T8#GNS221_U2_T8_h8)

question: What type of bowel prep is usually given right before a proctoscopy?

options.A: A 4-liter gallon prep
options.B: Total fasting for 48 hours
options.C: A cleansing enema
options.D: Oral magnesium citrate

explanation: Spot on! Because a proctoscopy only looks at the very end of the bowel, a quick cleansing enema just before the test is usually all it takes to clear the area.

question: What does 'psychological safety' mean for nurses working on a hospital ward?

options.A: All medical equipment is padded to prevent physical injuries
options.B: Staff can report errors and voice concerns without fear of punishment
options.C: Nurses never experience emotional stress during their shifts
options.D: Patients are locked inside their rooms to prevent accidental falls

explanation: Psychological safety means you feel safe speaking up about a mistake or sharing a worry without being yelled at. It helps everyone learn!

question: If a hospital ward wants the most accurate count of surgical infections, which method should they use?

options.A: Patient self-reporting through comment cards left in the waiting room
options.B: Annual surveys sent out to former patients via postal mail six months later
options.C: Passive surveillance by waiting for surgeons to submit written feedback forms
options.D: Active surveillance by reviewing lab results and patient charts directly

explanation: Well done! Proactively checking charts and lab results catches infections that busy doctors and nurses might miss through normal reporting.

question: Which medication is most commonly given to newborns right after birth to prevent eye infections?

options.A: Erythromycin 0.5% ophthalmic ointment
options.B: Hydrocortisone anti-inflammatory cream
options.C: Silver nitrate solution ten percent
options.D: Normal saline irrigation drops

explanation: Great job! Erythromycin ointment is the go-to choice in the delivery room because it safely stops gonococcal infections without causing heavy irritation.

question: When should you collect a midstream urine sample for a lab culture if the patient needs antibiotics?

options.A: On the final day of the antibiotic course
options.B: Forty-eight hours after starting antibiotics
options.C: It does not matter when the sample is collected
options.D: Before giving the very first dose of antibiotic

explanation: Always collect the sample first! If you start antibiotics before taking the sample, the drug will kill the bacteria in the lab dish and give you a false negative result.

question: What does cultural competence mainly ask of a home health nurse?

options.A: Convincing the family to adopt modern medical lifestyles
options.B: Speaking multiple local languages fluently
options.C: Accepting and respecting diverse family lifestyles and beliefs without judgment
options.D: Refusing to care for patients with unfamiliar cultural practices
